title: Shallow payload sharing still needs private mutation bookkeeping
applies_when: A shallow container copy shares mutable internal occurrence/index lists, or an append-in-place performance optimization intersects an earlier copy-on-write repair.
lesson: Separate user payload from container bookkeeping. A shallow copy can intentionally share nested payload objects without allowing top-level assignment or concatenation to alter the original's named entries. Trace every writer, not only index-renumbering methods: append-in-place can invalidate an earlier invariant that assignment always rebinds a fresh list. Test source-to-copy and copy-to-source assignment, accumulated names and concatenation alongside intentional nested sharing. Read both optimization and correctness histories before choosing a repair. Pyparsing's original PR650 tracked list ownership; its simplified upstream append combined with PR645's shallow occurrence-list sharing leaves these writers unprotected. Support the existing author and show the missing regression rather than claim a new optimization or silently reverse the accepted hot-path tradeoff.
avoid_when: Documented views and in-place APIs may intentionally share structure. Trace the consumer too: Pyparsing named lookup reads occurrence.result directly, not _toklist[offset], so a suspicious insert offset comparison alone does not prove it returns an inserted value. get_name and other offset consumers remain separate questions. Do not deep-copy opaque payloads, restore quadratic list concatenation, or eagerly clone every metadata list on a hot copy path merely because a narrow test passes. Original-author-head targeted tests are not a current-main rebase, full suite or performance qualification. A readable source example and public history establish the aliasing mechanism, not measured Scout conversion/recall, a universal fix or a portable speedup.

evidence.note: copy() duplicates only the outer _tokdict and intentionally shares occurrence lists; both __setitem__ branches append to an existing list in place. The copy docstring separately says contained ParseResults payloads remain shared. This supports the concrete writer/alias distinction, not all parser semantics.

Maintainer explicitly requests keeping the parsing hot path optimal. The final repair copies lists only in renumbering mutations; later discussion assumes assignment and concatenation already create fresh lists. Read that assumption against current code.

Original author proposed _own_keys tracking, including copy.copy serialization paths, to preserve semantics while avoiding quadratic append work. Maintainer incorporated an append-only simplification as 9671184 instead. Author timing claims are not our measurements or proof of current-head acceptance.
